voice.text: Good morning! You just woke up. [pause] Where is the sun right now? Low, near the hills? Or high overhead? Tap your guess.
<emphasis>Morning.</emphasis> The sun is LOW, over the side where it rises. [pause] Look — the tree's shadow is long.
<emphasis>Noon</emphasis> — lunchtime. The sun is HIGH overhead. [pause] Now the shadow is at its shortest.
<emphasis>Evening.</emphasis> The sun sinks LOW on the other side, where it sets. [pause] The shadow grows long again.
All day, the sun is the great warmer. [pause] It warms the LAND. It warms the AIR. It warms the WATER.

At night the sun is not gone. It never turns off. [pause] The Earth slowly turns, so the sun shines on the other side of the world. [pause] The sun is not alive — it doesn't follow you. [pause] In the morning, there it is again. Low, where it rises.
Where is the sun? [pause] Tap a sun spot in the sky, or tap an answer button.
You tracked the sun all day! [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. That low spot is where the sun rises — that's morning. [pause] Think about the time again.
Not quite. High overhead is the middle of the day — noon. [pause] Think about the time again.
Not quite. That low spot is where the sun sets — that's evening. [pause] Think about the time again.
Not quite. Morning sun is low — and low sun makes long shadows.
Not quite. Watch the tree: long, short, long. Shadows change all day.
Not quite. The shade blocks the sun's warmth. The sunny spot is the warm one.
Not quite. Try it outside — the sunny spot always feels warmer. The sun warms the land.
Not quite. The sun warms land, air, AND water. Sunny water turns warm.
Not quite. The sun never turns off. The Earth turns — night is our side facing away.
Not quite. The sun isn't alive. It doesn't sleep or follow you. The Earth turns.
Yes! [pause] Morning sun sits low, over the side where it rises.
Yes! [pause] At noon the sun is high overhead.
Yes! [pause] Evening sun sinks low on the sunset side.
Yes! [pause] When the sun is straight up, the shadow shrinks to its shortest.
Yes! [pause] Noon — high sun, short shadow.
Yes! [pause] The sun warms the land, so sunny sand gets warm.
Yes! [pause] The sun warms water too. Land, air, AND water.
Yes! [pause] The Earth turns — the sun keeps shining on the other side.
It's morning. Where is the sun?
When is the tree's shadow shortest?
At night, the sun…
Why does the sun seem to move across the sky?
What does the sun warm?
<soft>You can track the sun across the sky!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the sun's trip once more.
Lesson done! Now go outside with a grown-up and check your tree's shadow — morning, noon, and evening.
